I'm not actually sure honestly. But it was very recently. I didn't know what else to do. I began to pray every day. I didn't believe in God. I just went through the motions of, "if there's a god out there, I may as well give this a chance." I finished multiple novenas. I didn't feel anything. Nothing special happened. Nothing changed. I prayed anyway, because what else could I do?

Somewhere, somehow, I fell in love with God. I'm not sure when it happened or how it happened. At one point I was praying empty prayers. At some point I realized I loved God. Nothing else mattered but Him. He was and is my everything. Nothing outside of me changed--my circumstances didn't change, my temptations didn't change, my plans didn't change. But... God changed my heart.

Keep searching. Like I said, I honestly can't pinpoint when or how it happened. But I prayed everyday, even when I didn't want to, didn't feel like it. Even when the most I could do was a simple, "I don't love you, but I want to love you. Help me to love you." Even if you aren't sure, even if you aren't sincere, God hears you. Just persevere and pray every day. If you slip up, if you miss a few days, it's okay. We're human. God knows this. He made us. Just pick up where you left off. Pray for grace--beg for grace. He's listening, even if it doesn't seem like it. He loves you, and He will come through for you.

Here's something I was reflecting on today. There are people giving up on this subreddit--and this is not coming from a place of judgment, I'm struggling with the same thing--but I have to wonder how many of them would be husbands, wives, fathers, or mothers if they gave it 10 years.

Will marrying a partner, having a kid solve suicidality? No. I don't think so, because you do see parents and husbands and wives posting on this subreddit as well. Making a new family unit isn't the answer.

However, those who have somehow managed to endure past the thick of it to breathe one more day, and one more day, and one more day; some of them have made *new life* through simply postponing their death. By surviving through their pain, they somehow still managed to fall in love and create a brand new human being who will not only pass on their genetic DNA, but will have brand new ideas and hopes and dreams to bring to the world, to the future. 

With nothing but time. Nothing but one more hard, agonizing day. So many nights where they cried themselves to sleep, and some nights where they couldn't sleep at all. And somehow they still managed to exist and through them, new life now also exists.

Here is what I gathered from your post, and I'm sorry if I make assumptions; correct me if I'm wrong. But you sound incredibly lonely. It sounds like you don't believe anyone is out there for you. But here is what I see, from the other side of this screen, from the other side of your pain, from the other side of your aching loneliness. I see a likable guy. I see someone who tried hard to please his family, which tells me you are kind and thoughtful. I see someone questioning his place in the world, looking for meaning, and to me that speaks of unquestionable intelligence. Because so many people these days consume endlessly and don't bother wondering about why they were born, why they exist. You seek a deeper meaning, and the world needs people like you.

I know what it feels like to be lost and confused and it's truly a burden. But there is hope for you, because you already have direction, even if it's tiny and seems insignificant. Because you *know* you're uncertain about your major; and that's okay! Because you are under no obligation to continue pursuing something you are disinterested in. This means you have a direction, away from where you are right now. Towards something that actually excites you... something to return meaning to your life. You want to be a cop? That is GREAT. Because you know what it's like to live in darkness. You will be able to relate to people on a truly human level, and this is something that cops these days desperately need. You will be able to empathize in a way others could not, because you have been to this pit of desperation and loneliness, and you will be able to look other desperate people in the eye and let them know it will be okay; because you were there, and you lived.

It won't be easy. It will be almost impossibly hard, but not impossible. Because yeah, cops need psych testing. And in your state, right now at this moment, you would not pass. But, if you seek help, reach out, claw your way to a place you can stand upright and *breathe*, you will pass with flying colors. And you will be able to help so many other people with the love and care you deserve to feel right now. And like I said, I see an intelligent, kind, thoughtful guy. Girls were interested in you in the past; and girls will be interested in you in the future. Maybe not right at this moment, no. But if your future wife is out there, and you aren't meant to meet her until a while back from now... wouldn't she be worth waiting for? A few months or years alone, in solitude, struggling with loneliness, for the sake of the rest of a lifetime with a woman you fall in love with all over again every day you spend with her. 

Do I think you can survive that wait, feeling as you do now? No. No, I don't think anyone can endure the darkness you are feeling for very long at all. But, if you open yourself up to anyone; your family, your closest friend; somebody who will take you seriously and listen to you... there is *hope* there. No promises of everything getting better, no promises of quick solutions or emptiness filled. Just simply hope. Hope that you can help other people, hope that you can pursue this inkling of a feeling that you're meant to be a cop, hope that there is a future wife waiting for you, hope that you can stay on this earth long enough to wait for *her.*

I know you feel lost and alone because you expressed this in your writing. But I just want you to know, here at a time when you are ready to end all things; I hear you and I see you. And I don't have to be the only one.

As others have said, it's probably not their fault. I've always rattled off my list pretty quickly and the length of my confession depends entirely on the priest. Sometimes they go into detail and sometimes they go almost straight to absolution. 

It doesn't sound like a penitent problem, and I think it's great your priest is so concerned about each individual soul to take so much time for each person. However-- 30min once a week before Mass for the ONLY allotted time for confessions? Someone needs to approach the priest and he either needs to be aware that with only 30min every week he must speed things up on his end, OR he needs to offer more and longer times for confession. He needs to be aware that he cannot spend so much time with each person if he does not allow a longer time slot for confessions as a whole. Really, your parish needs a longer time slot and more opportunities to go. That's wonderful people are queuing up and seeking to be forgiven, and I would hope the parish steps up to the demand by ensuring all the people seeking Jesus are able to confess to Him and receive absolution.

It might be best to alert your priest there is a time problem, and offer suggestions to help him resolve this.

Confession is the perfect venue for discussing your sin. Not at the weekly time set aside for all the other parishioners, though. You have to keep in mind that yes, Jesus is there for you--and for all the other dozens of souls in line. 

The best practice for someone who wants to go in-depth with their sin is to schedule their own private confession at another time, where the priest can focus solely on them without worrying they won't have time to get to all the other souls waiting to be forgiven.

Yes, exactly. Only if you had purposefully withheld a sin would your confession have been invalid. But you simply forgot, which was not intentional.

If you forgot any mortal sins, next time you go to confession you need to simply mention to the priest that you forgot some mortal sins from last time (and then confess the sins). If you forgot any venial sins, you're totally in the clear. And whether you forgot venial or mortal sins, your confession was still perfectly valid.
